sanskrit_verse:
कामात् क्रोधाच् च लोभाच् च त्रिभ्यो यस्मात् प्रवर्तते।
त्रियोनिः कीर्त्यते तेन त्रयम् एतद् विवादकृत्॥
transliteration: kāmāt krodhāc ca lobhāc ca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate | triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayam etad vivādakṛt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Desire, anger, and greed are the threefold origin of all disputes; thus these three are declared as the root causes of conflict.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from consciousness clarity, not emotional impulse.
Causation arises from unregulated desire, anger, and greed within individual awareness.
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to recognize and transcend these impulses.
Restoration logic demands addressing the source—inner imbalance—not external blame.
Consciousness alignment requires dissolution of kama, krodha, and lobha through self-realization.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a dispute arises AND its root cause traces to unchecked desire, THEN initiate capacity-building protocols for emotional regulation.
IF a conflict manifests due to reactive anger, THEN assign completion process to restore inner equilibrium before reintegration.
IF greed drives action leading to discord, THEN activate consciousness-alignment mechanisms focused on non-possessiveness.
ALL disputes MUST be traced back to their causal triad (kama, krodha, lobha) prior to resolution.
NO adjudication shall proceed without verification of participant readiness for consciousness-based realignment.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any matter involving civil, commercial, or interpersonal conflict must first undergo analysis of whether it stems from kama, krodha, or lobha. Only upon identifying and initiating correction at this level may the case proceed. The threshold of responsibility lies in recognizing one’s own participation in these impulses and engaging in corrective alignment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyaya operates through pramana-based recognition that desire, anger, and greed arise sequentially from misidentification with limited self. As such, proportional responsibility rests not in assigning fault but in facilitating anupurvasaḥ — the sequential dissolution of these causes through conscious completion. This aligns fully with the non-punitive reality rule where justice restores harmony rather than inflicts consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Desire Completion Process: Guide individual through experiential realization of impermanence of objects of desire.
Activate Anger Dissolution Protocol: Engage breath-body-mind integration techniques until somatic charge resolves.
Implement Greed Transcendence Mechanism: Facilitate renunciation practices aligned with svadharma and contentment.
Assign Collective Reintegration Ceremony: Once internal triad is resolved, perform group acknowledgment and harmony renewal ritual.
Verify Consciousness Stabilization: Confirm participant has stabilized beyond reactive patterns before concluding legal process.
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: all disputes originate in desire, anger, and greed. Justice flows only when these roots are dissolved through consciousness restoration. There is no punishment, only realignment. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
